title: Where a restaurant phone number should appear
seoTitle: Restaurant phone number listing: where it should appear
description: Make sure your restaurant phone number appears in the right places, from search and maps to your website, delivery apps, and voicemail.
question: Where should my restaurant phone number appear so customers can actually call and place orders?
answer: Your restaurant phone number should appear everywhere customers decide whether to call: your website, Google Business Profile, Google Maps, delivery app profiles, social pages, receipts, menus, and voicemail greeting. Keep the same number consistent, make it tap-to-call on mobile, and use call forwarding if you want an AI phone host like ROAL to answer while your restaurant keeps its existing number.
summary: Put your restaurant phone number in the places customers already check, then make it easy to tap, call, and forward.
intro:
Your restaurant phone number should appear on your website, Google Business Profile, Google Maps, delivery app profiles, and anywhere customers look for a quick way to call. It should be the same number everywhere, easy to tap on mobile, and easy to forward when you want extra help answering calls.

If you use an AI phone host like ROAL, your existing number can stay the same. ROAL gives each location its own phone line and lets you forward your current number to it, so callers still dial the number they know while the phone host answers questions, takes orders, and sends clean tickets to the kitchen.

sections.h2: Where should my restaurant phone number appear first?
sections.body:
Start with the places customers check when they are hungry and ready to order. That usually means your website header, your Google Business Profile, Google Maps, your Facebook or Instagram bio, and any online menu or ordering page you control.

A simple rule works well: if a customer can see your hours, menu, or address, they should also see the phone number. Keep the number clickable on mobile. Use the same number everywhere so people do not wonder which line is right.

**Quick placement checklist**
- Website header and footer
- Google Business Profile
- Google Maps listing
- Mobile menu page
- Social profiles
- Printed menus and takeout bags
- Voicemail greeting

Example phone script line for your voicemail: "Thanks for calling Maria’s Pizza. For pickup orders, press 1 to place your order, or call back during business hours."

sections.h2: How do I make sure the number is easy to tap and call?
sections.body:
A restaurant phone number listing should do more than sit on a page. It should invite action. On mobile, the number needs to open the dialer with one tap. On desktop, it should still be easy to copy or click.

Use one plain format everywhere, like (555) 123-4567. Do not hide the number behind a picture. Do not put it only in a footer that takes too much scrolling to find. If customers need to search for your number, many will give up and move on.

**Simple formatting tips**
1. Put the number near the top of the homepage.
2. Repeat it near the menu and hours.
3. Make it bold or larger than the body text.
4. Add a short label like "Order by phone" or "Call for pickup."
5. Test it on your own phone.

Example line for your website: "Call to order pickup and delivery."

sections.h2: What should I do with my existing restaurant number?
sections.body:
Keep it. In most cases, the best move is to keep your current number and make it work harder. Customers already know it, and changing it can create confusion in Google, maps, receipts, and old flyers.

If you want help answering calls, forward your existing number to the line ROAL gives each location. You can forward all calls, or only when the line is busy or unanswered. Forwarding can be turned off any time. Always confirm the right code with your carrier and test with a real call, because codes vary by phone company and plan.

| Setup goal | What to do |
|---|---|
| Keep your number public | Use your current number on your website and profiles |
| Add backup answering | Forward calls to the ROAL line |
| Protect busy times | Forward only when busy or unanswered |
| Go back to normal | Turn forwarding off when needed |

ROAL can answer the call, take pickup and delivery orders from your live menu, and send a clean ticket to the kitchen screen. It also keeps the restaurant’s own number in place, which matters for repeat customers.

sections.h2: Where else should the number show up besides Google and the website?
sections.body:
A good restaurant phone number listing reaches the places that drive local traffic, not just your homepage. That means every public page where a guest might decide to call instead of order online.

Add the number to:
- Delivery app profile pages you control
- Reservation pages
- Catering pages
- FAQ pages for hours, parking, and large orders
- Receipts and takeout slips
- Door signage near the entrance
- Menus handed out in the shop

For example, if you run a deli, your catering page should show the number right next to the office platter section. If you run a pizza shop, the number should appear near your pickup special section. If someone is looking at a menu late at night, they should not have to hunt for it.

Example copy: "Need a large order or catering quote? Call us at (555) 123-4567."

sections.h2: How do I use the phone number to get more orders, not more headaches?
sections.body:
The number should bring in calls that are easy to handle. That means the greeting should set expectations, the menu should be current, and the person or system answering should know your hours, address, parking, and sold-out items.

A practical call flow looks like this:
1. Customer sees the number on Google or your website.
2. They call to place an order or ask a menu question.
3. The phone host answers, confirms the items, and quotes a ready time.
4. The kitchen gets a clean ticket.
5. The caller gets the right name and callback details.

ROAL can do that part by reading your public menu and hours, then answering common questions and taking orders from the live menu. It does not take card numbers over the phone, so payment still happens at pickup or however you already handle it.

Phone script example: "Thanks for calling. I can help with pickup orders, hours, and menu questions. For anything special, I’ll bring a staff member in."

sections.h2: How do I check if my phone number is listed correctly everywhere?
sections.body:
Do a quick audit once a month, and again any time you change hours, move locations, or update your menu. This takes less time than fixing confused callers later.

**Audit checklist**
- Call your own number from a mobile phone
- Test the tap-to-call button on your website
- Check Google Business Profile and Google Maps
- Look at your Facebook or Instagram bio
- Check your voicemail greeting for the right number and hours
- Confirm the number on printed menus, bags, and flyers
- Make sure old or wrong numbers are not floating around

If you need a faster way to compare costs, use the [phone host cost calculator](/tools/phone-host-cost-calculator) and [call forwarding codes by carrier](/tools/call-forwarding-codes). If you want to understand the setup better, see [How it works](/how-it-works) and [Questions owners ask](/faq).

takeaways: Put your restaurant phone number on your website, Google, Maps, menus, and social profiles.
Keep the same number everywhere so customers do not get confused.
Make the number tap-to-call on mobile and easy to find near hours and menu pages.
Use call forwarding if you want an AI phone host to answer while you keep your existing number.
Test your listing monthly so old numbers do not linger online.

faq.q: Where should a restaurant phone number be listed online?
faq.a: At minimum, list it on your website, Google Business Profile, Google Maps, and any pages where customers decide to call instead of order online. It should also appear on your social bios, catering pages, reservation pages, and FAQ pages for hours or parking. The goal is simple: if a guest is ready to call, the number should be visible right away.

faq.q: Should my restaurant keep the same phone number if I use call forwarding?
faq.a: Yes, in most cases you should keep the same public number. That avoids confusion for regulars, Google listings, printed menus, and old flyers. You can forward the existing number to another line, and turn forwarding off later if you need to.

faq.q: Do I need a different phone number for each restaurant location?
faq.a: Usually yes, each location should have its own number or its own forwarding setup so calls go to the right store. That makes hours, directions, and order handling clearer for customers. ROAL gives each location its own phone line automatically, then you forward your existing number to it if you want.

faq.q: How do I know if my restaurant phone number is listed wrong somewhere?
faq.a: Call your own restaurant from a mobile phone and check every place customers might look: website, Google, maps, social bios, and printed materials. If you see a wrong number, old line, or missing tap-to-call button, fix it right away. A monthly check is usually enough for most independent restaurants.
